title: Theo and the Inheritance
premise: Hazel Oyelaran, the coroner of the fading town of Marrow Creek, has spent years quietly correcting the record on deaths the police mislabeled as accidents. When a confession letter arrives for a man already buried—postmarked the day after his funeral—she realizes someone is using her town's dead to send messages, and that a ledger hidden in the cemetery's own records names every person who profited from those 'accidents,' including people she loves. As Hazel decodes the ledger with help from Theo, the teenage gravedigger's son who found the letter, she uncovers a protection racket run by the town's founding family and its sheriff. In the end, Hazel chooses justice outside the law: rather than hand the ledger to the corrupt sheriff, she publishes it through the dead themselves—engraving the truth into headstones and mailing copies to every family in Marrow Creek—forcing a reckoning the courts could never deliver, at the cost of her badge and her anonymity.
about_author: Petra Okonkwo is a former mortuary assistant from the American Midwest who writes mysteries about small towns that keep their secrets underground. She lives with her partner and an ill-tempered cat named Verdict.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She walks us through Marrow Creek's cemetery, introducing her habit of knowing the dead better than the living do, and closes out her third quietly corrected death certificate. Emotional beat: the comfort of invisibility, and its first hairline crack.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A confession letter arrives addressed to Dale Pruitt—buried two days prior—postmarked the day after his funeral. The handwriting is shaky, the confession specific: he didn't fall; he was pushed. Beat: dread blooming in a familiar place.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Reads Stones
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Sixteen-year-old Theo, the gravedigger's son, admits he found the letter tucked in Pruitt's freshly turned earth and mailed it back to himself first, curious. He wants in. Beat: reluctant alliance, sparks of found family.

chapters.title: Accident Number Four
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A fourth death—a diner cook, drowned in two inches of creek water—arrives on her table with injuries that don't match the story. Sheriff Brandt pressures her to sign quickly. Beat: the machinery of cover-up becomes visible.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. While re-inking faded cemetery plot records, Theo notices payments recorded as 'maintenance fees' dating back decades—amounts that match settlements no one ever heard about. Beat: the thrill of the hunt turning cold.

chapters.title: What the Dead Were Paid
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Cross-referencing the ledger with her files, Hazel finds each 'accident' victim's family received hush money from the Hollis family trust—the town founders. Beat: betrayal of everything she thought this town was.

chapters.title: Sheriff Brandt's Kindness
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. The sheriff, charming and menacing, warns Hazel off, revealing he knows about her three corrected certificates—and offers partnership instead of exposure. Beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Theo's Father Knows Something
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's father, the gravedigger, has been burying Hollis secrets for thirty years and begs Theo to stop digging. A violent argument ends with the father packing a bag. Beat: found family strained by blood loyalty.

chapters.title: Nine Names
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The ledger yields nine victims across four decades. One name stops her cold: her own mother, ruled a suicide when Hazel was nine. Beat: the investigation turns personal and the ground gives way.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Wasn't Grieving
chapters.summary: Hazel interviews Pruitt's widow, who lets slip she was paid twice—once before the funeral. Someone knew he'd die. Beat: premeditation confirmed; the case shifts from cover-up to murder-for-hire.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The records office catches fire overnight. Theo saves a partial photocopy hidden in his father's toolshed, but the original ledger pages are ash. Beat: loss, and the realization they're now targets.

chapters.title: An Offer Wearing a Smile
chapters.summary: Marguerite Hollis's POV. The matriarch invites Hazel to tea, offers to fund her retirement generously, and speaks of her mother with unsettling familiarity. Beat: power's velvet glove; Hazel understands her mother's death was purchased.

chapters.title: What Dad Buried Last
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's father returns drunk and terrified, confessing he was paid to move a body in 1994—Hazel's mother wasn't where the record says she is. Beat: horror reframing grief; a grave is a lie.

chapters.title: Exhumation at Midnight
chapters.summary: Hazel and Theo's alternating POV. They illegally exhale the wrong grave and find not Hazel's mother but a Hollis cousin everyone was told moved away. Beat: sacrilege as truth-telling; evidence in hand, law broken.

chapters.title: The Trap Closes
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Brandt arrests Theo for the exhumation and theft, dangling him as leverage: the ledger for the boy. Beat: Hazel's worst fear realized—her choices endangering her found family.

chapters.title: Confession, Second Draft
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, from a holding cell. Theo realizes the original confession letter's phrasing matches Marguerite Hollis's published memoir—he was quoting her book. Beat: the key turning; terror becoming clarity.

chapters.title: The Matriarch's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. We finally see inside her logic: payments as mercy, deaths as maintenance, a town as an inheritance to be pruned. She orders Brandt to make Hazel the tenth entry. Beat: chilling intimacy with corruption.

chapters.title: Running the Records
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel breaks into the county archive with help from the widow and the diner cook's daughter—victims' families she never knew she had. They recover the trust's full payment trail. Beat: found family forged in shared grief, racing the clock.

chapters.title: Ten Graves Deep
chapters.summary: Hazel and Theo escape a staged accident meant for them, hiding in the cemetery's receiving vault through a storm while Brandt searches. Beat: claustrophobic climax approach; Hazel decides the law won't save them.

chapters.title: The Truth in Stone
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Over one night, Hazel, Theo, and the families engrave the nine victims' real stories onto new markers and mail the ledger to every household in Marrow Creek. Beat: defiant, sacred, irreversible.

chapters.title: Reckoning Day
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. The town reads its mail; the courthouse steps fill; state investigators arrive ahead of Brandt's silencing attempt; Marguerite is taken, unrepentant, past the graves she bought. Beat: catharsis—justice arriving sideways but arriving.

chapters.title: What Hazel Keeps
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, epilogue. Stripped of her badge, Hazel opens a private practice verifying deaths for families the system failed, with Theo apprenticing beside her. Her mother's true marker stands corrected. Beat: quiet peace; invisibility traded for belonging.
